claims.claim_text: Indexed Thomas C Van Cleve is high-confidence matched to Bowdoin professor Thomas Curtis Van Cleve, a World War II Army intelligence officer.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact first and middle names, uncommon surname, intelligence service and indexed OSS context form a coherent identity bridge.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from exact name expansion, institutional career chronology and explicit World War II intelligence-officer service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The finding aid establishes Bowdoin employment before wartime service but does not specify the date of OSS accession.
claims.match_notes: The conclusion does not rely on the shared surname alone.

claims.claim_text: Thomas Curtis Van Cleve taught history and political science at Bowdoin College before his World War II intelligence service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Bowdoin's finding aid dates his teaching from 1915 to 1954 and states that World War II intelligence service interrupted that career.
claims.temporal_assessment: Bowdoin is the last documented civilian employer before wartime service; the exact OSS transition remains unproven.
claims.match_notes: Published as last civilian employer before wartime service, not as an explicit immediate transfer into OSS.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Ides Van Der Grac is high-confidence matched to architect and Army intelligence officer Ides van Waterschoot van der Gracht, later a leader of OSS Operation Melanie.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare name, matching major/captain officer trajectory, Army intelligence assignment and explicit OSS operation form a strong identity bridge.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from an exceptionally rare name, source-documented name expansion, military intelligence context and explicit OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Sources provide a 1940 architectural practice, an April 1943 Army assignment and 1944 OSS leadership.
claims.match_notes: The indexed spelling remains primary; the full documented spelling is retained as a variant.

claims.claim_text: Ides van der Gracht was an intelligence officer with the 345th Bombardment Squadron in North Africa in April 1943, before leading an OSS mission in 1944.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary AIA letter identifies the unit and role; a CIA-released report identifies his later OSS Operation Melanie leadership.
claims.temporal_assessment: Best-supported probable immediate military pathway; the sources do not give a formal transfer date into OSS.
claims.match_notes: Military assignment is not labeled a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: In 1940 Ides van der Gracht practiced architecture with Walter H. Kilham Jr. in New York.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary Architectural Forum project credits the eponymous architectural partnership; his 1943 letter describes having entered the Air Corps from architecture.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence rare-name and continuous profession match.
claims.temporal_assessment: This is the last documented civilian practice before Army Air Forces service; exact end date is not stated.
claims.match_notes: Classified as self-employment in an eponymous partnership rather than inventing an employee relationship.
